_source: docs/09 §11.4 'Tier word table for Tiers 2-5'; docs/10 §2 'Do not invent lore names, in code, in UI, or in asset filenames.'
_notes: One material word and one title word per tier, with the cloth line and the healer line
carrying their own, exactly as docs/09 §11.4's table is shaped. Every item name in tiers
2-5 is GENERATED from these words, which is why they are data and not literals.
TIERS 2-5 ARE PENDING AND THIS FILE DOES NOT NAME THEM. `pending: true` is the whole
point: tools/gen_items.gd stamps `name_pending` on every row of a pending tier and
refuses to call a tier finished, and docs/15 records the failure mode this avoids —
'Ship placeholders -> 300+ items named by accident'. The `candidates` below are the words
docs/09 §11.4 and docs/15 already wrote down as DISCUSSION CANDIDATES. They are recorded
here so the designer is choosing between rendered names rather than reading a blank table;
nothing reads them, and a generator that used one would be inventing lore.
TIER 1 IS ANSWERED, and its words are read off canon's own item names rather than
asserted: 'Iron Adventurer's Helm' and 'Blessed Adventurer's Circlet' in
data/items_t1_adventure.json, 'Reinforced Spellweave Robe' in docs/09 §10.2's cloth row,
'Raider's Boots' and 'Basic Raid Sword' in data/items_t1_raid.json — so `raid_adj` is 'Raid',
the {RaidTitle-adj} slot of docs/09 §11.3's `Basic {RaidTitle-adj} {WeaponNoun}`; it held 'Basic'
until 2026-09-15 and would have rendered 'Basic Basic Sword' (DESIGNER-02; corrected by W6-LEDGER).
ONE KNOWN WRINKLE, recorded rather than smoothed over: at Tier 1 the monk and rogue line
reads 'Reinforced Leather Vest', not 'Iron Leather Vest', so canon's T1 leather line uses
a fourth word that the generator's single `material` column does not have. It does not
bite today because Tier 1 is READ from the canon files and never generated — but a tier-2
leather piece will render as '<material> Leather Vest', and if the designer wants the
leather line to keep its own word, this table needs a fifth column and so does
FIVE COLUMNS PER TIER, PLUS THE LEATHER DECISION (2026-09-15, W6-LEDGER; CONTENT-04). tools/gen_items.gd
reads five word keys — material, cloth, healer, raid_title, raid_adj — not the two docs/09 §11.4 tabled
before this date, so every pending tier's `candidates` block now lists all five, with null where no
candidate was ever written down (cloth, healer, raid_adj). `leather` is the sixth: canon's T1 leather line
reads 'Reinforced', and the top-level `leather_column` records the one structural choice the designer
makes with the words — its own word per tier (then `leather` fills), or shared with `material` from Tier 2
on (the recommended default; nothing reads `leather` until it is chosen). The designer's page carries
the whole sheet as one answer line per tier.
THE ARENA IS A TIER KEY TOO (2026-09-15, W7-STAGE; CONTENT-26, CRITIC-C15, docs/15 Q-96 RESOLVED):
`scene` names the plate a tier's fights are shown on, per kind — {"adventure": …, "raid": …} — read
by ContentDB.tier_scene(tier, kind) and by nothing else; SceneStage.arena_for(encounter) takes it when
the tier row names one and otherwise applies Q-96's kind rule (E-slots in the dungeon, A/TR in the
cave). Tier 1 names both plates explicitly so the rule and the row agree; a pending tier carries no
`scene` and inherits the kind rule until a designer authors its plate (BL-100). A scene name here is
the JSON's basename under game/assets/scenes/, never a path: the content layer knows nothing of art.
PENDING TIERS CARRY NO WORD KEYS AT ALL, deliberately. tools/gen_items.gd falls back to the
token `TIER<n>` when a column is absent, so a generated name reads 'TIER2 Adventurer's Helm'
— unmistakably a placeholder. Empty strings were tried first and are worse: they render as
"'s Boots", which looks like a bug rather than like an unanswered question.

options: its own word per tier (the leather key fills)
leather_column.why: canon's T1 Monk/Rogue line already mixes Ironbound and Reinforced (docs/09 §11.3), so a shared metal word from Tier 2 is not a new inconsistency; the designer's page asks the question beside the twenty words.
